title.value: SharMiX: Adaptive Entropy Regularization via Sharma-Mittal Proximal Layers

abstract.value:
Layers grounded in Shannon–Boltzmann entropy well-known as softmax familly oversmooth tail evidence, whereas fixed‑sparsity transforms such as sparsemax are brittle; one‑parameter generalizations based on Tsallis or Rényi entropies (
-entmax) improve sparsity but still lack adaptive control. We present $\textit{SharMiX}
$, a two‑parameter family of activation/loss functions derived from Sharma–Mittal entropy that continuously interpolates the path  $\textit{softmax → entmax → sparsemax}$ while remaining fully differentiable. Treating both entropy parameters $(q;r)$
 as learnable, we derive closed‑form Jacobians with respect to inputs and to 
 via implicit differentiation, enabling drop‑in training with standard first‑order optimizers. On domains related datasets, SharMiX boosts metrics over competiting activations, converges faster, and achieves smoother sparsity transitions than one‑parameter entmax. SharMiX therefore provides a theoretically grounded, analytically tractable tool for adaptive sparse objectives in non‑convex deep‑network optimization.

TLDR.value: Two-parameter successor for softmax  based on Sharma-Mittal entropy, having pros of entmax\sparsemax: adaptive sparsity, improved calibration, closed-form Jacobian.
